Buying an apartment in Dushanbe today is possible on any budget — from a compact one-room apartment in Firdavsi to a penthouse in the center. The problem is different: there are many offers, and without a plan, it's easy to spend months on viewings or, worse, buy a property with problematic documents. Here is a proven course of action.

## Step 1. Calculate your real budget

Add 10–15% to the price of the apartment for related expenses: notary registration, state fees, moving, and minimal renovation even in a "ready" apartment. If you are taking a mortgage, get preliminary bank approval first, and only then go to viewings. This way, you won't fall in love with an apartment that the bank won't approve.

## Step 2. Choose a district for your lifestyle

Families with children are more likely to suit Shohmansur and the residential neighborhoods of Sino — schools, kindergartens, and parks are within walking distance there. For those working in the center, I. Somoni is more convenient: the commute takes minutes, but the price per square meter is higher. Firdavsi is a compromise: developed infrastructure and more affordable prices.

## Step 3. New development or secondary market

New developments offer modern layouts, new utilities, and installment plans from the developer, but the renovation is up to you, and sometimes you have to wait to move in. The secondary market means "move in and live" and an established courtyard, but hidden problems are possible: old wiring, worn-out pipes, utility debts.

## Step 4. Check the documents before the deposit

Ask for title documents, a certificate of no encumbrances and debts, and the consent of the seller's spouse if the apartment was bought during marriage. If minors are registered in the apartment, the transaction must be prepared especially carefully. This is the stage where the help of a realtor and a lawyer pays off completely.

## Step 5. Inspect the apartment during the day

In daylight, everything is visible: traces of leaks on the ceiling, the condition of the windows, the real illumination of the rooms. Check the water pressure, open all the taps, look at the meters. Talk to the neighbors — they will tell you more about the building than any advertisement.

If you don't want to go through this path alone, ROYAL HOME realtors take care of the selection, document verification, and bargaining. The first consultation is free.

Mortgages in Tajikistan are no longer exotic: housing loans are issued by several large banks, and rates start from 14% per annum in somoni (state program) and average 19–23%. We explain how the process works and what to pay attention to.

## What affects the rate

Three main factors: the down payment, the loan term, and confirmed income. The larger the down payment (usually from 20–30%) and the shorter the term, the lower the rate. An official salary or stable account turnover for an entrepreneur significantly simplifies approval.

## What documents are needed

Standard set: passport, income certificate for the last 6–12 months, documents for the selected apartment. If part of the income is remittances from abroad, check with the bank in advance how to confirm them: banks' practices vary.

## How long to wait for approval

With a ready package of documents, many banks give a preliminary decision in 1–2 working days. Next is the appraisal of the apartment and proceeding to the transaction, usually another week. In total, it is realistic to complete everything from the application to the keys in two weeks.

## Common mistakes of borrowers

First — taking the maximum amount approved by the bank: the payment should not exceed 40% of the family income, otherwise any force majeure will become a problem. Second — looking only at the rate and not reading the payment schedule and commissions. Third — taking out a mortgage on an apartment with unverified documents: the bank checks the property formally, the risks remain with the buyer.

Real estate in Dushanbe remains one of the most understandable ways to preserve and increase capital: the city is growing, rental demand is stable, and there are still fewer new high-quality buildings than people willing to live in them.

## 1. Center — I. Somoni

An investment classic: apartments near Rudaki Avenue and in the neighborhoods around the center are always in demand. Rent here is the most expensive in the city — expats, employees of international organizations, and businesses rent here. The entry threshold is high, but liquidity is also maximum: you can sell a central apartment quickly in any market.

The most active construction of recent years. Buying an apartment at the excavation stage from a trusted developer means earning on the price increase by the time the building is commissioned. The district of schools and kindergartens. Two- and three-room apartments here are rented by families for years — the tenant is stable, there is almost no downtime. Profitability is average, but predictable.

One-room apartments and studios near universities are rented out quickly and expensively in terms of square meters. The downside is seasonality and more frequent turnover of tenants.

## 5. Firdavsi — for growth

So far, prices are below the city average, but infrastructure is catching up: new roads, shopping centers, schools. The strategy "buy now, sell in 3–5 years" looks the most convincing here.

With long-term rent, an apartment in Dushanbe brings about 6–9% per annum plus the growth in the value of the property itself. Almost all problematic real estate transactions have one thing in common: the buyer took the seller's word for it and didn't check the documents. We break down the minimum checklist that protects against the most expensive mistakes.

## Title Documents

The main question: on what basis does the seller own the apartment? A sale and purchase agreement, a deed of gift, a certificate of inheritance — the document must exist in the original and match the seller's passport details. If selling by proxy, contact the owner personally and make sure the power of attorney has not been revoked.

## Encumbrances and Arrests

The apartment may be pledged to a bank, under arrest, or involved in a legal dispute. Technically, they may try to sell it to you, but you won't be able to register ownership — and getting your money back won't be easy. A fresh extract confirming the absence of encumbrances is mandatory.

## Registered Residents

A separate risk zone is people registered in the apartment, especially minors and those who refused privatization: deregistering them after the transaction can be extremely difficult. Demand that all residents be deregistered before signing the contract.

## Spouses and Heirs

An apartment purchased during marriage is joint property, even if registered to one spouse. Without the notarized consent of the second spouse, the transaction can be challenged. With inherited apartments, wait and check if other heirs might appear.

## Debts

Utility debts formally do not transfer to the new owner, but problems with service organizations will fall on you. Ask for certificates of no debts as of the transaction date.

An apartment in a new building is almost always handed over without finishing — and this is both freedom and a headache. The correct sequence of work saves up to a third of the budget, because nothing has to be redone.

## Determine the stage of readiness

"Rough" — bare walls, no screed, no wiring: plan for a full cycle of work. "Pre-finishing" — screed, plaster, and wiring are already there, only the final finishing remains. Both the budget and the deadlines depend on the stage: a full renovation of a two-room apartment usually takes 2–4 months.

## The correct sequence

First, everything "wet" and dirty: redevelopment, electrics, plumbing wiring, screed, plaster. Then tiles, ceilings, final wall coverings, floor coverings — and only at the end doors, baseboards, and furniture assembly. A classic mistake is to glue wallpaper before finishing work with the ceiling.

## Where you can't save

Electrics, pipes, and waterproofing of bathrooms — what is hidden under the finish. Redoing any of these systems after renovation costs more than doing it well right away. It is wiser to save on what is easy to replace: lamps, faucets, decor.

## Estimate and reserve

Add a 15–20% reserve to any estimate — unforeseen work always pops up in renovations. Fix agreements with the crew in writing: volume, deadlines, payment stages. Payment for completed stages disciplines better than any promises.

## "Turnkey" option

If you don't have time to manage the construction, consider a turnkey renovation with a contract and a guarantee. ROYAL HOME does renovations with a 2-year guarantee: a design project, an estimate before work begins, and weekly photo reports — you see what you are paying for.

“Which district is better?” is the most frequent question from our clients. The honest answer: there is no best district, there is one that suits your lifestyle. Let's compare the four main districts of Dushanbe.

## I. Somoni — the center

Pros: everything is nearby — work, restaurants, parks, main streets of the city. The highest status and the most expensive rent if you plan to lease. Cons: the price per square meter is noticeably higher than average, courtyards of old houses are cramped, parking is a constant issue.

## Sino — modern and growing

The main district for new buildings: new houses, spacious layouts, closed courtyards. A good choice for those who want modern housing and are ready for the fact that infrastructure is still being built in some places. Prices range from medium to high depending on the class of the building.

## Shohmansur — family-oriented

An established district with schools, kindergartens, bazaars, and clinics within walking distance. Courtyards are green, neighbors have known each other for a long time. The choice of new buildings is more modest, but the secondary market is rich and prices are moderate.

## Firdavsi — affordable and promising

The most affordable in terms of prices among the four. It is actively being built and acquiring infrastructure, transport links with the center are good. For a first apartment or an investment "for the future" — a very viable option.

## How to choose in practice

Make a list of three things that are critical for you: time to work, school for children, budget. Eliminate districts that do not meet at least one criterion, and look at apartments only in the remaining ones. One day with a realtor who knows the city replaces weeks of independent searches — come, we will show you the districts in person.

blogPosts.title: How to choose an apartment in Dushanbe: a step-by-step guide
blogPosts.content:
Buying an apartment in Dushanbe today is possible on any budget — from a compact one-room apartment in Firdavsi to a penthouse in the center. The problem is different: there are many offers, and without a plan, it's easy to spend months on viewings or, worse, buy a property with problematic documents. Here is a proven course of action.

## Step 1. Calculate your real budget

Add 10–15% to the price of the apartment for related expenses: notary registration, state fees, moving, and minimal renovation even in a "ready" apartment. If you are taking a mortgage, get preliminary bank approval first, and only then go to viewings. This way, you won't fall in love with an apartment that the bank won't approve.

## Step 2. Choose a district for your lifestyle

Families with children are more likely to suit Shohmansur and the residential neighborhoods of Sino — schools, kindergartens, and parks are within walking distance there. For those working in the center, I. Somoni is more convenient: the commute takes minutes, but the price per square meter is higher. Firdavsi is a compromise: developed infrastructure and more affordable prices.

## Step 3. New development or secondary market

New developments offer modern layouts, new utilities, and installment plans from the developer, but the renovation is up to you, and sometimes you have to wait to move in. The secondary market means "move in and live" and an established courtyard, but hidden problems are possible: old wiring, worn-out pipes, utility debts.

## Step 4. Check the documents before the deposit

Ask for title documents, a certificate of no encumbrances and debts, and the consent of the seller's spouse if the apartment was bought during marriage. If minors are registered in the apartment, the transaction must be prepared especially carefully. This is the stage where the help of a realtor and a lawyer pays off completely.

## Step 5. Inspect the apartment during the day

In daylight, everything is visible: traces of leaks on the ceiling, the condition of the windows, the real illumination of the rooms. Check the water pressure, open all the taps, look at the meters. Talk to the neighbors — they will tell you more about the building than any advertisement.

If you don't want to go through this path alone, ROYAL HOME realtors take care of the selection, document verification, and bargaining. The first consultation is free.

blogPosts.title: Mortgages in Tajikistan in 2026: banks, rates, documents
blogPosts.content:
Mortgages in Tajikistan are no longer exotic: housing loans are issued by several large banks, and rates start from 14% per annum in somoni (state program) and average 19–23%. We explain how the process works and what to pay attention to.

## What affects the rate

Three main factors: the down payment, the loan term, and confirmed income. The larger the down payment (usually from 20–30%) and the shorter the term, the lower the rate. An official salary or stable account turnover for an entrepreneur significantly simplifies approval.

## What documents are needed

Standard set: passport, income certificate for the last 6–12 months, documents for the selected apartment. If part of the income is remittances from abroad, check with the bank in advance how to confirm them: banks' practices vary.

## How long to wait for approval

With a ready package of documents, many banks give a preliminary decision in 1–2 working days. Next is the appraisal of the apartment and proceeding to the transaction, usually another week. In total, it is realistic to complete everything from the application to the keys in two weeks.

## Common mistakes of borrowers

First — taking the maximum amount approved by the bank: the payment should not exceed 40% of the family income, otherwise any force majeure will become a problem. Second — looking only at the rate and not reading the payment schedule and commissions. Third — taking out a mortgage on an apartment with unverified documents: the bank checks the property formally, the risks remain with the buyer.

## How we help

ROYAL HOME works with six partner banks: we select a program for your situation, help collect documents, and submit an application to several banks at once to compare conditions. The service is free for buyers of our properties.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 locations in Dushanbe for real estate investment
blogPosts.content:
Real estate in Dushanbe remains one of the most understandable ways to preserve and increase capital: the city is growing, rental demand is stable, and there are still fewer new high-quality buildings than people willing to live in them.

## 1. Center — I. Somoni

An investment classic: apartments near Rudaki Avenue and in the neighborhoods around the center are always in demand. Rent here is the most expensive in the city — expats, employees of international organizations, and businesses rent here. The entry threshold is high, but liquidity is also maximum: you can sell a central apartment quickly in any market.

## 2. Sino — new developments

The most active construction of recent years. Buying an apartment at the excavation stage from a trusted developer means earning on the price increase by the time the building is commissioned. It is important to look at the developer's reputation and the pace of construction, not just the price per square meter.

## 3. Shohmansur — family rentals

The district of schools and kindergartens. Two- and three-room apartments here are rented by families for years — the tenant is stable, there is almost no downtime. Profitability is average, but predictable.

## 4. Neighborhoods near major universities

One-room apartments and studios near universities are rented out quickly and expensively in terms of square meters. The downside is seasonality and more frequent turnover of tenants.

## 5. Firdavsi — for growth

So far, prices are below the city average, but infrastructure is catching up: new roads, shopping centers, schools. The strategy "buy now, sell in 3–5 years" looks the most convincing here.

## Simple math

With long-term rent, an apartment in Dushanbe brings about 6–9% per annum plus the growth in the value of the property itself. The key rule: profitability is calculated before the purchase, not after. Our specialists will calculate the payback of a specific apartment for free — come with an address, leave with numbers.

blogPosts.title: Documents when buying an apartment: what to check so as not to lose money
blogPosts.content:
Almost all problematic real estate transactions have one thing in common: the buyer took the seller's word for it and didn't check the documents. We break down the minimum checklist that protects against the most expensive mistakes.

## Title Documents

The main question: on what basis does the seller own the apartment? A sale and purchase agreement, a deed of gift, a certificate of inheritance — the document must exist in the original and match the seller's passport details. If selling by proxy, contact the owner personally and make sure the power of attorney has not been revoked.

## Encumbrances and Arrests

The apartment may be pledged to a bank, under arrest, or involved in a legal dispute. Technically, they may try to sell it to you, but you won't be able to register ownership — and getting your money back won't be easy. A fresh extract confirming the absence of encumbrances is mandatory.

## Registered Residents

A separate risk zone is people registered in the apartment, especially minors and those who refused privatization: deregistering them after the transaction can be extremely difficult. Demand that all residents be deregistered before signing the contract.

## Spouses and Heirs

An apartment purchased during marriage is joint property, even if registered to one spouse. Without the notarized consent of the second spouse, the transaction can be challenged. With inherited apartments, wait and check if other heirs might appear.

## Debts

Utility debts formally do not transfer to the new owner, but problems with service organizations will fall on you. Ask for certificates of no debts as of the transaction date.

blogPosts.title: Renovating an apartment in a new building: where to start and how much to budget
blogPosts.content:
An apartment in a new building is almost always handed over without finishing — and this is both freedom and a headache. The correct sequence of work saves up to a third of the budget, because nothing has to be redone.

## Determine the stage of readiness

"Rough" — bare walls, no screed, no wiring: plan for a full cycle of work. "Pre-finishing" — screed, plaster, and wiring are already there, only the final finishing remains. Both the budget and the deadlines depend on the stage: a full renovation of a two-room apartment usually takes 2–4 months.

## The correct sequence

First, everything "wet" and dirty: redevelopment, electrics, plumbing wiring, screed, plaster. Then tiles, ceilings, final wall coverings, floor coverings — and only at the end doors, baseboards, and furniture assembly. A classic mistake is to glue wallpaper before finishing work with the ceiling.

## Where you can't save

Electrics, pipes, and waterproofing of bathrooms — what is hidden under the finish. Redoing any of these systems after renovation costs more than doing it well right away. It is wiser to save on what is easy to replace: lamps, faucets, decor.

## Estimate and reserve

Add a 15–20% reserve to any estimate — unforeseen work always pops up in renovations. Fix agreements with the crew in writing: volume, deadlines, payment stages. Payment for completed stages disciplines better than any promises.

## "Turnkey" option

If you don't have time to manage the construction, consider a turnkey renovation with a contract and a guarantee. ROYAL HOME does renovations with a 2-year guarantee: a design project, an estimate before work begins, and weekly photo reports — you see what you are paying for.

blogPosts.title: Districts of Dushanbe: where to live — a comparison for buyers
blogPosts.content:
“Which district is better?” is the most frequent question from our clients. The honest answer: there is no best district, there is one that suits your lifestyle. Let's compare the four main districts of Dushanbe.

## I. Somoni — the center

Pros: everything is nearby — work, restaurants, parks, main streets of the city. The highest status and the most expensive rent if you plan to lease. Cons: the price per square meter is noticeably higher than average, courtyards of old houses are cramped, parking is a constant issue.

## Sino — modern and growing

The main district for new buildings: new houses, spacious layouts, closed courtyards. A good choice for those who want modern housing and are ready for the fact that infrastructure is still being built in some places. Prices range from medium to high depending on the class of the building.

## Shohmansur — family-oriented

An established district with schools, kindergartens, bazaars, and clinics within walking distance. Courtyards are green, neighbors have known each other for a long time. The choice of new buildings is more modest, but the secondary market is rich and prices are moderate.

## Firdavsi — affordable and promising

The most affordable in terms of prices among the four. It is actively being built and acquiring infrastructure, transport links with the center are good. For a first apartment or an investment "for the future" — a very viable option.

## How to choose in practice

Make a list of three things that are critical for you: time to work, school for children, budget. Eliminate districts that do not meet at least one criterion, and look at apartments only in the remaining ones. One day with a realtor who knows the city replaces weeks of independent searches — come, we will show you the districts in person.
